notes: Mossad now finds the right calendar event for a call: from the call's link, from the meeting's name in the Google Meet window, and from who spoke. A call that is not on your calendar no longer takes the name of another event, and your meetings of the last two weeks are checked again. Your points for a person now show in your one-on-ones with them, not in group meetings: a group meeting shows how many there are.

When Mossad sees the call change in your browser, two calls back to back now become two meetings, each with its own notes. The recording never stops for this: Mossad makes the two meetings after the call. Delete now removes everything of a meeting: its recording and notes, its tasks, its chats, your points for it, and the voice samples learned from it. The people stay.

A person whom Mossad added from your Gemini notes now shows where they came from, and one switch in Settings turns that off: everyone already added stays. When you move a meeting to another profile, your points for that meeting go with it.

The call that you record is now at the top of the window on every page: one click opens it. When Mossad cannot see your mute button, it says that you were muted when it last looked, and it keeps your mic. Save a point for any online meeting on your calendar, also one that happens once: a point that you did not raise in a one-on-one waits for the next time you see that person. With Google connected, the people who spoke in Gemini notes join your People list with their address, only when your directory leaves no doubt, and a person you deleted stays gone. A network that blocks your server now says so.

Profiles: keep work calls and personal calls apart on your Mac and your iPhone, each with its own meetings, people, keys, sync, and connection for AI apps. The profile that you are not in still finishes its meetings. A meeting that went to the wrong profile moves to the right one, and during a call you can say which profile it is for. A phone call that you record on your iPhone becomes a meeting: share the recording to Mossad. Undo after Transcribe again restores the whole meeting. Update the Mac and the iPhone app together.

ChatGPT, Claude, and other web AI apps can now read much more through your own server: your recurring meetings with their history and open items, each meeting's numbers, your analytics, your bookmarks, and the coach's cards and goal. Your upcoming meetings stay on your Mac.

Tell Mossad to do things: add a point for a meeting, add a task, bookmark a moment, with a receipt and Undo. Your AI apps can read everything in the app: people, recurring meetings, your points, the coach, and more.

More room to read on every page, with one spacing scale for the whole app. Pages use a wide window well: a full-width top and centered content. A transcript no longer drops a line beside two bookmarks.

A quick chat panel over any app, with a shortcut you can change. Your points during the call, checked off as you raise them. Recurring meetings by weekday, and on a calendar. The list shows your next two work days. A headset that changes mode can no longer stop a recording.
More room in chat answers and questions.

Ask the call you are on: a chat with the live call, with quick questions. A new chat design with times that open the moment. More accurate names in the live transcript. A finding's audio stops when you answer the card.
Back and Forward in the main window. Recurring is first under Meetings, with search and a filter. 45 days of upcoming meetings, by day. Anonymous usage statistics, with a switch in Settings.
